pageCache.pageTitle: Meet our People - Barnsole Primary School
pageCache.text:
Meet our People
Text
The best way to understand what it is like to work at Barnsole Primary School is to hear from the people who experience it every day.
Our staff come from a range of backgrounds, roles and career stages, bringing different experiences, skills and perspectives to our school community.
Some colleagues have been part of Barnsole for many years, while others have joined more recently and brought new perspectives to the school. Together, they represent the breadth of experience, dedication and enthusiasm that makes Barnsole such a rewarding place to work.
If you are considering joining us, we hope their experiences give you a genuine insight into life at Barnsole.
Real Staff Voices
Every colleague's experience is different, but together these reflections offer an honest insight into what it's like to work at Barnsole.
Here is what some of our colleagues say about working here:
"The team I work with are fantastic, so supportive and helpful. We work brilliantly as a team, in my opinion. Within my school, I know who I can go to if I need support or advice. The leadership team listens to our opinions and acts upon them. Again, if I need support from leadership, I know this will happen without judgment. They support our work-life balance, which makes work manageable and enjoyable."
"The school are very considerate about staff wellbeing and take active measures to make sure that as teachers we are supported at work. Leadership check in with staff regarding our opinions of workload and new initiatives to make sure they are manageable."
"I love working at Barnsole, the staff all care about the children, they are happy to support any ideas that come with the happiness of the children. I feel at home at Barnsole and have been welcomed into the school like family, they are always happy to take on any ideas I have to further better the children's experience at school and make their time at school fun!"
"I enjoy working at Barnsole Primary School because colleagues are very supportive of one another and help each other if unsure. The Maritime Academy Trust offer a wide range of courses for professional development, HR and Finance are very helpful."
"I like the people I work closely with and that makes the day to day job feel more positive and supportive. I feel like this year especially things have shifted in a positive way with regards to workload and work life balance. I’ve had opportunities for career development and progression. I’ve felt supported when I’ve needed it for medical or personal reasons"
expander
The Difference Our People Make
Every day, Barnsole colleagues make a positive difference to the lives of children and families.
Whether they are teaching in the classroom, supporting pupils' wellbeing, working with parents or helping the school run smoothly behind the scenes, every role contributes to creating an environment where children feel safe, inspired and ready to succeed.
It is the commitment, professionalism and care shown by our staff every day that helps Barnsole continue to thrive and makes it such a rewarding place to build a career.
For many colleagues, it is this shared sense of purpose and commitment to the community that makes working at Barnsole so rewarding.
Take the Next Step in Your Journey
If the experiences shared by our colleagues have given you a sense of what makes Barnsole special, we would be delighted to hear from you.
Explore our current opportunities or join our Talent Community to stay connected with future roles at Barnsole Primary School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Part of Maritime Academy Trust - Barnsole Primary School
pageCache.text:
Part of Maritime Academy Trust
text
Barnsole Primary School is proud to be part of Maritime Academy Trust — a family of schools united by a shared commitment to providing excellent education and creating opportunities for children, staff and communities to thrive.
Being part of the Trust means colleagues benefit from the strengths of both worlds: the relationships, identity and community connections of Barnsole, alongside the expertise, collaboration and development opportunities available across a wider organisation.
Through Maritime Academy Trust, staff are connected to a professional network where expertise is shared, practice is continually developed and colleagues are supported at every stage of their careers.
columns
WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOUR CAREER
As part of Barnsole and Maritime Academy Trust, you will have access to opportunities and support that extend beyond your own school, including:
Professional networks across Maritime Academy Trust
Opportunities to collaborate with colleagues across different schools and phases
Trust-wide training, leadership development and professional learning programmes
Clear pathways for career progression across a family of schools
Access to specialist expertise, coaching and mentoring
Opportunities to contribute to Trust-wide projects and communities of practice
This means you can build your career within a school where people know and value one another, while benefiting from the expertise, support and career pathways available across the Trust.
COMMUNITY ROOTS, WIDER OPPORTUNITIES
One of the things that makes Barnsole special is the balance between belonging and opportunity.
You are part of a school with more than 125 years of history, strong relationships with local families and a deep commitment to the community it serves. Colleagues work together with a shared purpose: helping every child achieve their potential.
Alongside this, Maritime Academy Trust provides access to wider professional networks, development opportunities and career pathways that can support you throughout your career.
This combination allows you to enjoy the familiarity and purpose of an established community school, while continuing to grow, learn and progress within a wider family of schools.
Explore Opportunities Across Maritime Academy Trust
Whether you're planning your next career move or looking ahead to future opportunities, discover the support, professional development and career pathways available across Maritime Academy Trust.

Wraparound Care
text
Our wraparound care is our Breakfast Club and After School Club which are run by members of our School staff. Breakfast Club is based in the Junior site with entrance through the main office. After School Club is based in the Infant hall with collection via the door nearest to the Nursery building.
Breakfast Club
7:30am - 8:40am (Term time only)
Session Price: £6 each morning
Children are provided with breakfast and are supervised with reading, games and activities.
Breakfast served is: toast, cereal, fruit and yoghurts
Please speak to the school office to book a place for your child.
After School Club
At Barnsole we offer a daily After School Club for all year groups, except Nursery, which is based on the Infant site. For further information call 01634 333400 or email the school office at: office@barnsole-maritime.org
For After School Club emergencies after 4pm, please call 07717 638299.
Session 1: up to 5.00pm is £7.00
Session 2: up to 6.00pm is £13.00 (Mon-Thurs Only)
Please note on a Friday, our After School Club finishes slightly earlier at 5.00pm.
Please note there is a £5 charge for every 15 minutes for late picks up after 6pm.
Parents are required to provide healthy snack for their child.
Please speak to the school office to book a place for your child.
Payment is made via the MyChildatSchool app.

House System
text
At Barnsole Primary School we believe that all children should be given a sense of belonging within our community through encouragement to be positive role models and part of a supportive team.
Our House System creates friendly competition, good work and behaviour, encourages teamwork, and provides opportunities to take on responsibilities and brings everyone in the school together.
Every child who attends our school (except Nursery) is assigned to one of our four 'house teams'. Each house is made up of pupils from different year groups from Reception up to Year 6.
There are four house teams at Barnsole, which are led by a House Captain and a Deputy. The four houses are called Adams, Gordon, Invicta and Medway.
expanders
Adams House Team
William Adams (1564–1620) was an English navigator and the first known Westerner to reach Japan in 1600. Born in Gillingham, Kent, Adams had strong connections to the Medway area, where he trained as a shipbuilder and gained maritime skills. After a long voyage with a Dutch fleet, Adams arrived in Japan, where he became a trusted advisor to the shogun, Tokugawa Ieyasu. He helped establish trade relations between Japan and Europe and was granted the rank of samurai. His pioneering journey marked the start of early relations between Japan and the West, making him a significant historical figure.
Gordon House Team
Major General Charles George Gordon (1833–1885), also known as "Gordon of Khartoum," was a renowned British military leader and national hero. Known for his courage, leadership, and humanitarian work, Gordon played significant roles in conflicts across the British Empire, including the Crimean War, China, and Sudan. His last stand in Khartoum during the Mahdist War made him a symbol of British heroism and sacrifice. Gordon has a strong connection to the Gillingham and Medway area through his service as Commandant of the Royal Engineers at Chatham from 1865 to 1871. During his time there, he was known for his charitable efforts, particularly in helping the poor and supporting local education, leaving a lasting legacy in the region.
Invicta House Team
"Invicta" is a Latin word meaning "unconquered" or "undefeated." It is famously used as the motto of the county of Kent, symbolising the county's resilience and determination in the face of adversity. The motto is said to have originated from Kent’s resistance to William the Conqueror's rule in the 11th century. The people of Kent successfully negotiated favorable terms after the Norman invasion, reflecting the county’s spirit of strength and independence. The link to Gillingham and Medway comes from the motto's historical association with the region, representing the unyielding spirit of its people. By naming one of our house teams "Invicta," we celebrate this enduring resilience and local pride, inspiring students to embody these qualities in their school life and beyond.
Medway House Team
The Medway Queen is a historic paddle steamer with strong ties to the Gillingham and Medway area. Built in 1924, she became famous for her heroic role during World War II, particularly in the Dunkirk evacuation of 1940. The Medway Queen rescued over 7,000 soldiers during Operation Dynamo, making multiple trips across the English Channel despite facing enemy fire. The boat was originally based in the River Medway and operated as a pleasure steamer, serving local communities. Today, she stands as a symbol of courage and resilience, reflecting the rich maritime heritage of Gillingham and the Medway region.
text
Responsibility & Leadership
As part of the wider curriculum at Barnsole we understand the importance of providing more opportunities for our older pupils to take responsibility and develop leadership skills. At the beginning of each academic year assemblies are held in order for the children to elect their House Captains. One pupils from Year 6 is elected House Captain for each House Team.
The job of the house captains is to take responsibility for the leadership, direction and organisation of their house throughout one academic year. In addition to the house captain, one deputy house captain is also elected for each house to support the house captain in their duties.
House Captains & Deputies
House Points
The children are given the opportunity to win house points for their team. House points are awarded for children exhibiting our school values and going 'above and beyond' what is normally expected of them in school. Please see below for the latest house point scores.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from our Headteacher - Barnsole Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from our Headteacher
text
I would like to welcome you to Barnsole Primary School. Barnsole is a school where every day we feel a deep sense of pride in our children and all they achieve. Our children are happy at school and enjoy learning. They have excellent attitudes to their learning, behave well and care for one another.
We believe that children should have an exciting start to their school life, and this is represented though our ambitious and creative curriculum. We take a holistic approach to the education of our children. As a values-based school, relationships are at the heart of all we do. We place great emphasis on developing the whole child through focusing on language, good manners, honesty, showing respect, cooperation, and collaboration, taking responsibility for themselves and others.
We celebrate the success of all the children and are always endeavouring to seek new ways to improve the quality of learning opportunities for everyone. From when the children start in nursery they are taught to value the learning process. They have a deep sense of pride in their learning and what they have achieved, they are also able to talk clearly about what they need to do to further progress.
The staff at Barnsole are established, highly skilled and work brilliantly as a team. They always put children first and strive for excellence in everything they do. All staff have a positive, ‘can do’ attitude and adopt a solution-focused approach to overcome obstacles and enable everyone to achieve their full potential.
We expect nothing but the absolute best from all our children, staff and parents. We aim to always be a school where children and adults are proud to come every day.

For more than 125 years, Barnsole has been at the heart of the Gillingham community, supporting generations of children and families. Today, we remain a school built on strong relationships, high expectations and a commitment to helping every child succeed.

pageCache.text:
Life at our School
text
What it feels like to work here
No two days at Barnsole are quite the same.
One morning might begin with outdoor learning in Forest School, while another could involve supporting a school performance, celebrating a cultural event or helping pupils prepare for a sporting competition. Across our infant and junior sites, staff play an active role in creating engaging experiences that help children learn, grow and succeed.
From the moment you join us, you'll become part of a team that shares ideas, celebrates success and works together to provide the very best experiences for children. Our experienced colleagues create an environment where people feel encouraged to contribute, learn from one another and continue developing throughout their careers.
Life at Barnsole extends beyond the classroom. Staff regularly contribute to the wider opportunities that enrich school life, from educational visits and enrichment activities to family events and community celebrations supported by our active PTA.
Across the school, you'll see diversity celebrated through learning, events and everyday interactions, creating an environment where everyone feels welcomed, respected and able to be themselves.
You can expect:
icons
Days that are varied, rewarding and full of opportunity
Opportunities to be involved in Forest School, educational visits and enrichment activities
Strong partnerships with families through community events and our active PTA
Collaboration across our infant and junior sites
Children who are enthusiastic, curious and eager to learn
Colleagues who willingly share ideas and expertise
Leaders who are visible, approachable and invested in your success
text
For many colleagues, Barnsole is a place where every day brings the opportunity to make a positive difference, work alongside dedicated professionals and be part of a school that is continually looking ahead.
Staff Wellbeing & Support
At Barnsole, we recognise that staff wellbeing plays an important role in creating a positive experience for both colleagues and pupils.
We are proud of the positive working environment that exists across the school, where people work together, celebrate successes and look out for one another. Our experienced team and approachable leaders help create an environment where staff feel listened to, valued and supported.

text
Introduction to the Project
At Barnsole Primary School we recognise the importance of digital skills in today’s modern world. We understand the necessity of preparing our pupils for a future where digital proficiency is paramount. Barnsole and Maritime Academy Trust have been working in collaboration. Our 1:1 Chromebook Project, initiated in October 2021, is a testament to our commitment to bridging the digital divide and fostering an environment where technology enhances learning and personal development.
Project Aims
The project's core objectives are to:
Enhance learning opportunities through peer interaction
Provide more problem-solving tasks
Foster creativity and critical thinking
Encourage self-learning and independent exploration

Attendance and Holidays
text
At Barnsole Primary School, a pupil's regular attendance is every parent's responsibility and legal duty.
We work in close partnership with pupils, parents, carers and the wider community to improve all aspects of attendance and punctuality.
expanders
Reporting Absences
If your child is unable to attend school, you must inform us by 9.00am on each day of absence by one of the following methods:
Email: office@barnsole-maritime.org or absence@barnsole-maritime.org
Telephone the school on 01634 333400 by 9:00am
Via the MyChildAtSchool app
Please note we require a specific reason for all absences in order to complete our statutory attendance registers.
Reason for absence. Specific reason for absence.
Any absences that are not reported will be followed up with a telephone call and/or email. If we are unable to make contact, we may undertake a home visit as part of our statutory safeguarding procedures.
Please refer to Section 6 Authorised and Unauthorised Absences of Barnsole’s Attendance Strategy Policy, which is administered in conjunction with Medway Council.
Medical and Planned Absences
Where possible, we ask that medical or dental appointments are made outside of school hours. We recognised, however, that this is not always feasible.
For any planned absence, such as hospital, doctor, or dental appointments, parents and carers must complete an Absence Request Form and attach a copy of the appointment card or letter. Hard copies of the form are available from the School Office.
NHS Live Well Website
This NHS website has a comprehensive page about common illnesses (see below. This can be used as a reference to see if your child should come to school.
NHS Live Well - is-my-child-too-ill-for-school
Holidays During Term Time
Holidays taken during term time are not authorised and may result in a penalty notice. Families who take holidays during school time will be referred to Medway Council, which works closely with the school.
The law states that parents and carers do not have a legal right to take their child out of school for holidays during term time.
Penalty Notices for Unauthorised Absence
With effect from August 2024, the UK national policy on unauthorised absence changed. The key points are:
The penalty charge is £160 per parent, per child.
If paid within 21 days the charge is reduced to £90.
Penalties and prosecutions apply to each parent with parent responsibility, for each child.
Attendance missed and the impact on pupil's learning
In line with the new guidance from the DfE, schools are encouraged to regularly inform parents about their child’s attendance and absence levels. Here is the guidance from the UK Government
Working together to improve school attendance.
Attendance Record and Lessons Missed
95% attendance means 50 missed lessons. This means a child missed about 10 days or 2 weeks of lessons in the school year.
90% attendance means 100 missed lessons. This means a child misses four weeks of lessons in the school year.
85% attendance means 150 missed lessons. This means the child misses almost 6 weeks of lessons in the school year.
80% attendance means 200 missed lessons. This means the child misses over 7 weeks of lessons in the school year.
75% attendance means 250 missed lessons. This means the child misses about 9 weeks of lessons in the school year.
Punctuality
Arriving 5 minutes late every day adds up to over 3 days lost each year, that's 20 lessons missed
Arriving 15 minutes late every day adds up to 2 weeks absence a year, thats 55 lessons missed
Arriving 30 minutes late every adds up to 19 days absence a year, that's 123 lessons missed
*Please note, these calculations are approximate, based on how the terms fall each calendar year.

Bad Weather Advice
text
It is always our aim to keep the school open. However, there may be times when severe weather conditions make it unsafe for travel or the premises unsafe for children and adults in which case the school may need to be closed.
If we need to close the school due to hazardous conditions we will notify parents via MCAS app, School Website and our Facebook page.
